chunks: And Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn 'Ali al-Naqid narrated to me, saying: Abu Harun al-'Issi [al-'Absi] narrated to me from Abu al-Ashhab Ja'far ibn Hanan [Hayyan], from Khalid al-Raba'i, who said: He narrated to me from someone who heard Ka'b saying:

The first person to curse the killer of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) was Ibrahim, the Friend of the Merciful; he cursed him and ordered his children to do so, and took a covenant and pledge from them. Then Musa ibn 'Imran cursed him and ordered his nation to do so. Then Dawud cursed him and ordered the Children of Israel to do so. Then 'Isa cursed him and frequently said: 'O Children of Israel! Curse his killer, and if you meet his days, do not sit away from him, for the martyr with him is like the martyr with the prophets, facing forward not turning back [facing forward not turning back]. And it is as if I am looking at his place, and no prophet but that he visited Karbala and stood upon it and said: 'Verily you are a place full of goodness; in you will be buried the shining moon.'

key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيمُ خَلِيلُ الرَّحْمَنِ: Ibrahim, the Friend of the Merciful

ai.seo_question: Who were the first prophets to curse the killer of Imam Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the cosmic significance of Karbala by tracing the curse upon Husayn’s killers back to the primordial covenant of Ibrahim, thereby linking Shia devotion to the lineage of all prophets. It highlights the unique status of the martyr as being in the presence of the prophets, a concept that reinforces the Shia belief in the intercessory power and eternal vigilance of the Ahl al-Bayt. The narration also serves as a theological validation of Karbala as a sacred site visited by every prophet, emphasizing its role as a focal point of divine love and remembrance.
